title: qe evidence manifest
description: Public manifest schema for <ledger-root>/evidence/<run-id>/manifest.json (root .wicked-qe/, or a legacy .wicked-testing/). See docs/EVIDENCE.md. ADDITIVE-FIELD POLICY: this schema (and its nested objects) sets `additionalProperties: false` for producer integrity. The manifest grows additively under `manifest_version` semver — minor bumps add optional fields only (docs/EVIDENCE.md §7). Consumers validating against a vendored copy of this schema MUST gate on `manifest_version` and ignore unknown fields rather than reject them; do not enforce `additionalProperties: false` against payloads carrying a higher minor `manifest_version` than the schema copy you hold.

verdict.description: The recorded verdict. `additionalProperties: false` here is a PRODUCER-INTEGRITY guard, not a consumer contract: it stops the qe producer from silently emitting unknown keys. The manifest evolves ADDITIVELY under `manifest_version` (semver) — minor bumps add OPTIONAL fields and never change or remove existing ones (see docs/EVIDENCE.md §7). STRICT external validators MUST NOT vendor this `additionalProperties: false` verbatim against payloads from a newer producer; gate on `manifest_version` and ignore unknown fields instead, or a future additive field (as `equivalence` was in 1.1.0) will be falsely rejected.

equivalence.description: Optional baseline-match facet. Present when a behavior-preserving change was judged against a captured baseline (golden-master / contract / data-reconciliation / perceptual). A green run is not sufficient evidence of a faithful reproduction — this names the baseline-match as a typed, queryable fact.

baseline_ref.description: Path or identifier of the captured baseline artifact.

baseline_sha.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the baseline, for provenance.

diff_count.description: Number of differences found vs. the baseline.

tolerance.description: Allowed diff threshold; matched is true when diff_count <= tolerance.

matched.description: Whether the fresh output matched the baseline within tolerance.

scenario_evidence.description: OPTIONAL manifest-2.1 block (minor bump — 2.0.0 manifests without it stay valid): the campaign evidence shape proven by the 2026-08 studio E2E campaign, plus the first-class claim_level enum. `status` is the EXECUTOR'S CLAIM in the verdict taxonomy — never the verdict of record (the top-level `verdict` block stays that). Deliberately `additionalProperties: true`, unlike the producer-integrity guards elsewhere in this schema: the authoritative twin validator (wicked-ledger lib/manifest.mjs validateManifest, mirrored here in lib/manifest.mjs) tolerates unknown keys inside this block by the additive doctrine, so a newer producer's optional key must not be rejected. The honest-cap invariant — the overall claim_level may never be STRONGER than the weakest leg in `legs` (certify the journey, not the proxy; self-capping further is allowed) — is not expressible here and is enforced by the twin JS validator.

status.description: Executor's claim, in the verdict taxonomy.

claim_level.description: Overall claim level for the scenario (floor of the legs): certified = the user journey itself was exercised and verified; machinery-verified = a disclosed proxy verified the machinery, not the journey; skipped = not executed (disclosed).

legs.description: Per-leg claim levels (e.g. an API-substituted acceptance leg).

reason.description: Why the leg is capped/skipped (disclosed substitutions).
